title: Les conditionnels : zero, first, second
summary: Si + présent, si + prétérit : réalité, possibilité, hypothèse. Et la règle d'or : pas de will après if.

blocks.text: *If + présent, présent.* *If you heat ice, it melts.* Se traduit par « quand » ou « si » équivalents.
*If + présent, will + verbe.* *If it rains, we will stay at home.*
*If + prétérit, would + verbe.* *If I had more time, I would learn Spanish.* (je n'en ai pas, donc c'est irréel)
Avec to be au second conditionnel, on emploie **were** pour toutes les personnes : *If I were you, I would call him.*

items: *unless* = if … not : *Unless you hurry, you'll miss the train.*
*as long as / provided that* = à condition que : *You can use it as long as you return it.*

blocks.en: If you press this button, the machine stops.
blocks.fr: Si tu appuies ici, la machine s'arrête.

blocks.en: If I find the file, I'll send it.
blocks.fr: Si je trouve le fichier, je l'enverrai.

blocks.en: If I won the lottery, I would travel.
blocks.fr: Si je gagnais au loto, je voyagerais.

blocks.en: I wouldn't do that if I were you.
blocks.fr: À ta place, je ne ferais pas ça.

blocks.text: **Piège** : jamais de *will* ni de *would* directement après *if*. *If it **rains**, …* (pas « if it will rain »).

exercises.q: If it rains, we ___ at home.
If I ___ rich, I would buy a boat.
If I ___ more time, I would travel.
___ you hurry, you'll miss the train.

options: If it will rain, we stay.
If it would rain, we'll stay.

exercises.q: If I were you, I ___ call him.
If she ___ (come), we'll start the meeting.
If I ___ (win) the lottery, I would travel.
If you ___ (not / hurry), you will be late.
If I ___ you, I'd ask for help. (to be)
If it ___ tomorrow, we won't go. (rain)
Remets les mots dans le bon ordre.
answers: If it rains we will stay at home
